data: {"content_index":0,"item_id":"","logprobs":[],"output_index":0,"sequence_number":446,"text":"Recommended city: **Tokyo, JP**.\n\n**15:00 — Establishing full-body portrait**  \nUse the mild start, **20°C, 20% precipitation, 45% cloud cover, 11 kph wind**, for a clean wide shot. Frame the long blue coat head-to-toe against stone, concrete, or steel. Keep the katana angled upward to catch silver highlights, echoing the reference image’s blue/silver styling and controlled, aristocratic mood.\n\n**15:30 — Coat silhouette walk-in**  \nStage a slow forward walk with the coat open just enough to reveal the darker inner layers and warm lining. The **11–12 kph wind range from 15:00–16:00** should give slight hem movement without losing the sharp, narrow silhouette.\n\n**16:00 — Sword-draw detail**  \nAt **19°C, 25% precipitation, 50% cloud cover, 12 kph wind**, move to a tighter three-quarter shot. Place the katana diagonally across the frame, emphasizing the silver blade against the deep blue coat and dark clothing.\n\n**16:45 — Reserved profile pose**  \nUse the increasing cloud softness before 17:00 for a stern side profile. Keep the sword sheathed and vertical behind the body, reinforcing the calm, threatening restraint visible in the reference.\n\n**17:15 — Dynamic coat-and-blade frame**  \nWith **18°C, 30% precipitation, 55% cloud cover, 13 kph wind at 17:00**, capture a controlled turn so the coat hem moves while the blade remains steady.\n\n**18:00 — Blue-hour final mood shot**  \nAt **17°C, 30% precipitation, 60% cloud cover, 12 kph wind**, shoot a darker, colder portrait with rim light on silver hair and katana.\n\n**Weather contingency:** because precipitation rises to **30% at 17:00 and 18:00**, keep a covered concrete or arcade location nearby; winds of **13 kph at 17:00** and **12 kph at 18:00** are manageable but still require secure sword handling.","type":"response.output_text.done"}
